children.title: Interior Orders Review to Reduce Barriers to Federal Energy Development
children.description_medium: On February 3, 2025, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum signed orders directing the department to review policies that burden energy development and identify authorities that could expedite permitting and leasing.  The Interior Department described the orders as an effort to facilitate energy development on federal lands.
children.description_long: On February 3, 2025, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum signed orders directing the department to review policies that burden energy development and identify authorities that could expedite permitting and leasing. The Interior Department described the orders as an effort to facilitate energy development on federal lands. This event is the department-wide policy direction and is distinct from the later Wyoming lease sale. The supplied official release and Secretary’s Order support the date and the stated review objective; they do not establish the original card’s claims about a specific acreage near Yellowstone or Grand Teton or about migration-corridor overlap. The February 2025 Interior orders describe a department-wide review and direction to facilitate development; they are not the lease transaction. The later BLM releases document a specific completed Wyoming sale, including the difference between acreage offered and acreage actually leased. That final reported acreage is about 114,439, not the roughly 250,000 acres described in the original card. The supplied releases do not support the card’s claims that the sale area was all near Yellowstone or Grand Teton or that a stated amount overlapped migration corridors. No geographic or ecological effects are inferred here.
children.date_uncertainty: Event dates are identified in the supplied reporting; publication dates may be later.

children.title: BLM Leases About 114,439 Wyoming Acres in June Oil and Gas Sale
children.description_medium: On June 9, 2026, the Bureau of Land Management reported that it had leased about 114,439 acres in its Wyoming oil and gas lease sale, generating $34. 7 million in receipts.  BLM’s sale announcement had listed 108 parcels totaling 119,595 acres; the completed sale’s reported leased acreage was therefore smaller than the acreage offered.
children.description_long: On June 9, 2026, the Bureau of Land Management reported that it had leased about 114,439 acres in its Wyoming oil and gas lease sale, generating $34.7 million in receipts. BLM’s sale announcement had listed 108 parcels totaling 119,595 acres; the completed sale’s reported leased acreage was therefore smaller than the acreage offered. This June transaction is separate from Burgum’s February 2025 orders to review federal energy policies. The supplied BLM releases support the acreage and receipt figures. They do not establish that a 250,000-acre block was leased, that the land was all near Yellowstone or Grand Teton, or that the specified migration corridors were affected. The February 2025 Interior orders describe a department-wide review and direction to facilitate development; they are not the lease transaction. The later BLM releases document a specific completed Wyoming sale, including the difference between acreage offered and acreage actually leased. That final reported acreage is about 114,439, not the roughly 250,000 acres described in the original card. The supplied releases do not support the card’s claims that the sale area was all near Yellowstone or Grand Teton or that a stated amount overlapped migration corridors. No geographic or ecological effects are inferred here.
